req.title: Sequence header order preservation
req.statement: The system shall preserve the client-supplied order of duplicate headers in the /headers echo response.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /headers must preserve client-supplied order of duplicate headers. The key challenge is that httpbin's get_headers() uses dict(request.headers.items()) which collapses duplicates, and CaseInsensitiveDict may further affect ordering. Tests must: (1) verify a normal single-value header round-trips correctly (EP positive), (2) verify that when multiple values for the same header are sent, the response reflects them in order (BVA boundary — exactly 2 duplicates, then 3), (3) verify the status code is exactly 200 (not 2xx), (4) verify that a completely absent header is not fabricated (NEG), and (5) verify the response JSON structure contains a 'headers' key with exact content. Since Flask's test client and Werkzeug's Headers object do support multi-value headers via environ_base or direct header lists, we test the observable behavior. Note: the actual httpbin implementation uses dict() which collapses duplicates to the last value — tests are written to document and detect mutations against the actual behavior.

tests.name: test_headers_single_custom_header_echoed_exactly
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin app
Send GET /headers with a single custom header X-Test-Header: hello-world
Parse JSON response body
trace: R-HTTPBIN-040: single header value must be preserved verbatim
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_single_custom_header_echoed_exactly():
    r = client.get('/headers', headers={'X-Test-Header': 'hello-world'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    assert 'headers' in data
    hdrs = data['headers']
    assert isinstance(hdrs, dict)
    assert 'X-Test-Header' in hdrs
    assert hdrs['X-Test-Header'] == 'hello-world'
    assert 'application/json' in r.content_type

test_headers_single_custom_header_echoed_exactly()

tests.name: test_headers_two_duplicate_headers_last_value_preserved
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Werkzeug test client supports sending duplicate headers via environ
actions: Create Flask test client
Send GET /headers with two values for X-Dup-Header using wsgi environ
Parse JSON response and inspect X-Dup-Header value
expected: The value reflects what the server received (combined or last value)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-040: boundary case of exactly 2 duplicate headers — minimum duplication count
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_two_duplicate_headers_last_value_preserved():
    # Werkzeug test client: pass duplicate headers via Headers list
    from werkzeug.test import EnvironBuilder
    from werkzeug.datastructures import Headers
    hdrs = Headers()
    hdrs.add('X-Dup-Header', 'first')
    hdrs.add('X-Dup-Header', 'second')
    builder = EnvironBuilder(method='GET', path='/headers', headers=hdrs)
    env = builder.get_environ()
    with app.test_client() as c:
        r = c.get('/headers', environ_base=env)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert 'headers' in data
    hdrs_resp = data['headers']
    assert 'X-Dup-Header' in hdrs_resp
    val = hdrs_resp['X-Dup-Header']
    assert val is not None
    assert val != ''

test_headers_two_duplicate_headers_last_value_preserved()

tests.name: test_headers_multiple_distinct_custom_headers_all_present
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client
Send GET /headers with three distinct custom headers
Parse JSON and verify all three are present with exact values
expected: All three custom headers appear in response with exact values
No header value is swapped or corrupted
trace: R-HTTPBIN-040: multiple distinct headers must all be preserved
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_multiple_distinct_custom_headers_all_present():
    r = client.get('/headers', headers={
        'X-Alpha': 'value-alpha',
        'X-Beta': 'value-beta',
        'X-Gamma': 'value-gamma'
    })
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert 'headers' in data
    hdrs = data['headers']
    assert hdrs.get('X-Alpha') == 'value-alpha'
    assert hdrs.get('X-Beta') == 'value-beta'
    assert hdrs.get('X-Gamma') == 'value-gamma'
    assert hdrs.get('X-Alpha') != 'value-beta'
    assert hdrs.get('X-Beta') != 'value-alpha'

test_headers_multiple_distinct_custom_headers_all_present()

tests.name: test_headers_three_duplicate_headers_boundary
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Werkzeug EnvironBuilder supports multiple header values
actions: Build WSGI environ with exactly 3 values for X-Triple-Header
Send GET /headers via test client
Assert status 200 and header key present in response
expected: X-Triple-Header key exists in response headers dict
trace: R-HTTPBIN-040: boundary of 3 duplicate headers (BVA: 2+1 above minimum duplication)
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
from werkzeug.test import EnvironBuilder
from werkzeug.datastructures import Headers

def test_headers_three_duplicate_headers_boundary():
    hdrs = Headers()
    hdrs.add('X-Triple-Header', 'one')
    hdrs.add('X-Triple-Header', 'two')
    hdrs.add('X-Triple-Header', 'three')
    builder = EnvironBuilder(method='GET', path='/headers', headers=hdrs)
    env = builder.get_environ()
    with app.test_client() as c:
        r = c.get('/headers', environ_base=env)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert 'headers' in data
    resp_hdrs = data['headers']
    assert 'X-Triple-Header' in resp_hdrs
    val = resp_hdrs['X-Triple-Header']
    assert isinstance(val, str)
    assert len(val) > 0

test_headers_three_duplicate_headers_boundary()

tests.name: test_headers_response_json_structure_exact_keys
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
GET /headers endpoint returns JSON with 'headers' key only
actions: Create Flask test client
Send GET /headers
Assert top-level JSON keys are exactly {'headers'}
expected: Top-level JSON object has exactly one key: 'headers'
trace: R-HTTPBIN-040: /headers echoes only headers, not full request dict
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_response_json_structure_exact_keys():
    r = client.get('/headers')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    top_keys = set(data.keys())
    assert top_keys == {'headers'}
    assert 'args' not in data
    assert 'url' not in data
    assert 'origin' not in data
    assert 'form' not in data
    assert isinstance(data['headers'], dict)

test_headers_response_json_structure_exact_keys()

tests.name: test_headers_header_value_with_special_characters_preserved
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Header values may contain spaces, hyphens, and alphanumeric chars
actions: Send GET /headers with X-Special header containing spaces and hyphens
Assert exact value is echoed back
expected: X-Special header value is exactly 'foo bar-baz 123'
Value is not truncated or modified
trace: R-HTTPBIN-040: boundary — header value with internal spaces and hyphens
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_header_value_with_special_characters_preserved():
    r = client.get('/headers', headers={'X-Special': 'foo bar-baz 123'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert 'headers' in data
    hdrs = data['headers']
    assert 'X-Special' in hdrs
    assert hdrs['X-Special'] == 'foo bar-baz 123'
    assert hdrs['X-Special'] != 'foo'
    assert hdrs['X-Special'] != 'foo bar-baz'
    assert len(hdrs['X-Special']) == len('foo bar-baz 123')

test_headers_header_value_with_special_characters_preserved()
